entries.german:
Witigo von Krumau schenkt dem neuen Cistercienserkloster zu Hohenfurt seinen Antheil an dem sogenannten Klosterwald.

In nomine sancte et indiuidue trinitatis amen. Quoniam eorum que geruntur in tempore, obliuio solet memoriam resecare, necesse est, ea tam testium quam scripture munimine perhennari. Nos igitur Witigo de Krvmbenowe notum facimus et constare uolumus presentium inspectoribus uniuersis, quod de consensu et expressa uoluntate uxoris nostre Sibille liberorumque nostrorum cenobio in Hohenwrt ordinis Cysterciensis, quod diuina inspirante gracia ad honorem sancte perpetueque uirginis dei genitricis Marie ob remedium anime sue Woko patruelis noster, marsalcus videlicet Boemie, de nouo fundare et construere in communi nostra possessione inchoauit, eam partem silve que nos iure hereditario contingebat, ut ipsius boni propositi et remunerationis diuine participes simus et nominis fundatoris, per manum domini Johannis venerabilis episcopi Pragensis in dedicatione eiusdem eeclesie dedimus in perpetuum pleno iure exceptione qualibet pretermissa, metas eiusdem predicto cenobio legitimas distiuguentes. Hec autem sunt mete: Nemus ex altera parte Wlte in occidentali parte attingens uiam illam que ducit in Helfenberch, in orientali parte transiens riuum quendam qui uocatur minor Wltawitz, et pratum Zbyadel inclusiue, ita quod idem pratum ad cenobium integraliter pertineat; et meta in riuulo Mokri nomine terminetur, et incipiens a flumine Wlta dirigitur ascendendo usque ad ortum riuuli iam predicti et inde per montem Hradisch in minorem WItawitz reuertitur ex directo, et ascendit in illo riuo usque ad altitudinem silue Boemiam et Bawariam diuidentem. Ut autem predicta robur habeant firmitatis presentem paginam scribi fecimus et sigilli nostri munimine roborari. Testes autem qui aderant sunt: Dominus Johannes prenotatus venerabilis episcopus Pragensis ecclesie. Dominus Heinricus et Wernhardus fratres de Schowenberch. Wernhardus et Heinricus eiusdem tituli fratres minores. Dominus Gerbertus. Dominus Liupoldus. Habelo. Andreas. Prehtlo. Chonradus de Turdelinge. Benada. Benysius. Bvdylaus purchrauii de Rosenberch, et alii quam plures. Datum et actum in Hohenwrt anno domini M o CC o viiij o Kal. Junii. Indictione XV.

Siegel: Gut erhaltenes dreieckiges, an gelbrother Seide hängendes Siegel in w. W. - Ein aufrecht einherschreitender einfach geschwänzter Löwe hat vor sich die fünfblätterige Rose. S. Vitigonis. De. Crhvmuovve. Vergl. XXIII.
entries.english:
Witigo von Krumau gives the newly founded Cistercian monastery of Hohenfurt his share of the so-called monastery forest.

In the name of the holy and indivisible Trinity, amen. Since forgetfulness usually cuts short the memory of things done in time, they must be perpetuated by the protection of both witnesses and writing. We, Witigo de Krvmbenowe, therefore make known to all who see these presents that, with the consent and express will of our wife Sibille and our children, we have given in perpetuity, with full right and without exception, to the Cistercian monastery at Hohenwrt the part of the forest belonging to us by hereditary right. Our paternal cousin Woko, marshal of Bohemia, inspired by divine grace, has begun to found and build this monastery anew on our common property, in honor of Mary, holy and perpetual virgin and mother of God, for the salvation of his soul. We make this gift through the hand of Herr Hans, the venerable bishop of Prague, at the dedication of the church, so that we may share in his good purpose, the divine reward and the name of founder. We establish the lawful boundaries of the grant to the monastery as follows.

The woodland lies on the other side of the Wlta, reaching westward to the road leading to Helfenberch and eastward across a stream called the lesser Wltawitz, including the meadow Zbyadel, so that the whole meadow belongs to the monastery. The boundary ends at the stream called Mokri; beginning at the Wlta it runs upstream to the source of that stream and from there straight back over Mount Hradisch to the lesser Wltawitz, then ascends that stream to the height of the forest dividing Bohemia from Bavaria.

To give these things lasting force we have had this document written and strengthened with our seal. The witnesses present are the aforesaid Herr Hans, venerable bishop of the church of Prague; Herr Heinrich and Wernhard, brothers de Schowenberch; the younger brothers Wernhard and Heinrich of the same name; Herr Gerbert; Herr Leopold; Habelo; Andreas; Prehtlo; Konrad de Turdelinge; Benada; Benysius; Bvdylaus, Burggraf de Rosenberg; and very many others. Done and given at Hohenwrt in the year of the Lord [text unclear], on the ninth day before the Kalends of June, in the fifteenth indiction.

The well-preserved triangular seal in white wax hangs from yellow-red silk. It shows an upright striding lion with a single tail, with a five-petalled rose before it. Its legend reads “S. Vitigonis de Crhvmuovve.” Compare no. XXIII.
